content:
Best practice is to just unsubscribe from Gmail's "All Mail" pseudo folder. It's not relevant to a standards-based email agent like Thunderbird, and it just tends to confuse the user, as you discovered.

To Unsubscribe, right-click on the Gmail account name in the Folders List and choose "Subscribe" from the pop-up context menu. This will show all the available IMAP folders. Remove the check mark beside "All Mail" and the folder will no longer be visible in Thunderbird.

content:
Unfortunately, there are many documented ways to transfer a profile, and some are problem-prone. If the transfer was done outside of thunderbird all should be there. Here are suggested steps:

BACKUP

  1. ensure thunderbird is not running
  2. enter %appdata% in search window on task bar and press Enter key
  3. this should open windows file explorer in Appdata\roaming folder
  4. highlight the Thunderbird folder and copy to external media

RESTORE

  1. ensure thunderbird is installed, run once, and NOT running
  2. enter %appdata% in search window on task bar and press Enter key
  3. delete the thunderbird folder
  4. you should be in Appdata\roaming folder , copy&paste the exported Thunderbird folder there.
  5. start thunderbird and all should be there

This process, by using windows file explorer, ensures that every component is transferred. This especially applies to POP accounts, as their files are on the PC and readily copied. If the old profile is still available, we can assist. Posting screenshot of the old profile's folder for the POP account will be a good start, plus a screenshot of the current profile's POP account folder. Let us know what guidance you need there.

content:
I think this is probably more a problem with your graphics system than with Thunderbird specifically. One Thunderbird setting that might help would be to disable its use of hardware acceleration. That setting can be found at <Settings | General>, scroll all the way to the bottom and disable the "Use hardware acceleration when available" option.

You might try playing around with the system graphics driver settings, in particular, any hardware acceleration settings, even if only for a temporary test. And check for updated drivers.
